question: A 20-year-old G1P0 woman at 12 weeks estimated gestational age presents to the obstetric clinic for the first prenatal visit She admits to being unsure of whether to keep or abort the pregnancy but now has finally decided to keep it. She says she is experiencing constant fatigue. Physical examination reveals conjunctival pallor. Her hemoglobin level is 10.1 g/dL. Which of the following additional features would likely be present in this patient?

paths: (Iron deficiency)-MANIFESTATION_OF->(uptake)-PROCESS_OF->(Structure of nail of toe)-LOCATION_OF->(Longitudinal split nail)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Iron deficiency -> Anemia -> Fatigue -> 80% CHAIN: Anemia -> Conjunctival pallor -> 70% CHAIN: Anemia -> Low hemoglobin level -> 90% CHAIN: Iron deficiency -> Pica -> 60% CHAIN: Iron deficiency -> Onychorrhexis -> 50% CHAIN: Iron deficiency -> Increased Transferrin Saturation -> 40% CHAIN: Iron deficiency -> Decreased TIBC -> 80%
enhanced_information: In a 20-year-old pregnant woman with iron deficiency anemia presenting with fatigue and conjunctival pallor, additional features likely include pica and onychorrhexis. Increased transferrin saturation and decreased TIBC may also be present.
analysis: In a pregnant woman with iron deficiency anemia presenting with fatigue and conjunctival pallor, common additional features include pica and onychorrhexis. While exercise tolerance may be reduced due to anemia, it is not a specific feature associated with this condition. Increased transferrin saturation and decreased TIBC are more likely to be present in iron overload conditions rather than iron deficiency anemia.
